Article Title: Goyal: Pull down barriers, allow easy movement to professionals
Article Text:
Piyush Goyal at Brics Business Forum

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Friday called for dismantling of trade barriers by Brics nations while urging them to link payment systems and trade in each other's local currency."We should open our markets for each other's products, including raw material and critical minerals. Our supply chains will be resilient when they run both ways, with non-tariff measures imposing higher import costs, in fact much more than the tariffs themselves," the minister said at Brics Business Forum.He called for streamlining regulatory and customs processes while also promoting services trade. "Let us open our services market for each other in the real sense, let professionals move easily across borders and make it easier to recognise each other's professional qualifications," the minister said.The comments come amid several countries holding up visas for Indian professionals and some like China mounting curbs on the export of many items while denying market access to goods from parts of the world.Pointing to initiatives taken by govt in laying out digital public infrastructure, Goyal said, "Today, it (UPI) is also accepted in 11 countries and I would urge Brics member countries and partner countries to link our payment systems, trade in each other's local currencies, make digital trade global and build together for the future emerging technologies."External affairs minister S Jaishankar called upon member nations to work towards addressing economic challenges by ensuring transparent trade and investment practices. "The common thread is how to make it easier for businesses in our countries to find more partners, access more markets, connect supply networks and convert complementarities into viable commercial partnerships," the EAM said, while pointing to geopolitical tensions.
Article Summary: Commerce and industry minister piyush goyal calls for dismantling of trade barriers by brics nations. He urges them to link payment systems and trade in each other's local currency. Comments come amid several countries holding up visas for indian professionals.

Article Title: Counting Discounts
Article Text:
How good is that online deal? We’ll know from Jan 1

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For years, UK consumer group “Which?” has found that many Black Friday deals are not really bargains. A shop may say a product has been cut from £500 to £400, but the product may never have actually sold for £500. Last year, none of the deals checked by the group was the cheapest price that product had been sold for in the previous 12 months.You may have seen something similar during festive sales in India. A product you have been waiting to buy during a Diwali sale may suddenly become more expensive when the sale begins. The “discounted” price may even be the same as, or higher than, its earlier price.The good news is that this should change on e-commerce platforms in India from January 1. Under new rules, when a seller announces a discount, it will also have to show the product’s “prior price”. This means the lowest price at which the product was sold on that platform during the 30 days before the discount was announced.This gives shoppers a simple way to check whether a discount is real. Without such a rule, it is easy to be fooled when big sale signs and huge discounts create excitement.Other major markets already have similar protections. In the US, the Federal Trade Commission says a “former price” used in an advertisement must be a genuine price.California says it must have been the normal market price within the previous 90 days. The European Union introduced a similar rule in 2022, using a 30-day price history. Its rule also applies to shops, not just online sellers.India should do the same. Online shoppers can use price-tracking websites to check whether a deal is genuine. But if a shop puts a “60% off” sign on a shirt, there is no easy way to know whether it was really sold at the higher price before. A discount should be a real saving, not just a clever trick.
Article Summary: When a seller announces a discount, it will also have to show the product’s ‘prior price’ this means the lowest price at which the product was sold on that platform during the 30 days before the discount was announced. The european union introduced a similar rule in 2022.

Article Title: Now, you can port FASTag from one bank to another
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Vehicle owners can now port their FASTags from one bank to another - much like the portability process for a mobile-phone number - with NHAI Friday rolling out the 'One Tag' framework. Nearly a dozen major banks, including SBI, ICICI and Airtel Payments Bank, have joined the tag's portability system.The move will allow users dissatisfied with their current FASTag issuer to switch to another participating bank without buying a fresh tag or replacing the existing one.Govt is also set to roll out an annual local pass for residents living within a 20-km radius of a toll plaza at a discounted price of around Rs 1,500. Currently, local passes are issued on a monthly basis, while the FASTag annual pass is valid for travel across the NH network.Minister Nitin Gadkari said the FASTag portability can be done through Rajmarg Yatra app. More than 98% of toll collection on the NH network is now done through FASTag.
Article Summary: Nearly a dozen major banks, including sbi, icici and airtel payments bank, have joined the tag's portability system. The move will allow users dissatisfied with their current fastag issuer to switch to another participating bank without buying a fresh tag or replacing the existing one.

Article Title: 'Trade barriers rising globally, India building bridges': PM Modi at Brics business forum
Article Text:
Trade barriers rising globally, India building economic bridges: PM Modi at BRICS Business Forum

Brics is a grouping of 11 major economies.

India seeks deeper economic role within Brics

Supply-chain resilience becomes a key priority

Infrastructure and strategic technologies

UPI as India's digital infrastructure model

Brics seeks greater business-to-business engagement

Brics members and partner countries now account for over 40% of the global GDP.

Why Brics matters to India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday positioned India as a bridge-builder in an increasingly fragmented global economy, saying the country is responding to rising trade barriers by expanding free-trade partnerships, strengthening supply chains and creating new avenues for businesses across the BRICS grouping.Addressing the Leaders' Session of the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi, PM Modi said the global trading environment is becoming more difficult as countries increasingly turn to tariffs, restrictions and other barriers to protect domestic industries. Against this backdrop, he said, India is pursuing greater economic integration by negotiating and signing trade agreements with a growing number of countries.“Today, while trade barriers are rising globally, India is building economic bridges. Since 2014, we have entered into free trade agreements with nearly 40 countries,” PM Modi said.The Prime Minister's message was aimed not only at highlighting India's expanding trade network but also at presenting the country as a stable and increasingly attractive destination for investment at a time when global businesses are trying to reduce their dependence on concentrated supply chains.“Our approach remains focused on reducing barriers and expanding opportunities for businesses,” PM Modi said.PM Modi also used India's Brics presidency to push for greater economic cooperation among the 11-member grouping.Rather than limiting Brics cooperation to government-to-government engagement, India is seeking to create networks that allow companies, startups and smaller businesses to access new markets, investment and technology.Under India's chairship, new cooperation networks have been established in areas including agriculture, healthcare, skills development and smart grids. These initiatives are intended to translate the political and economic weight of BRICS into practical opportunities for businesses.India has also launched the Brics Incubator Network, Brics MSME Portal and Brics Startup Innovation Fund.These initiatives are particularly significant for startups and micro, small and medium enterprises, which often face greater difficulties than large corporations in entering overseas markets, finding investors and establishing business partnerships.“To connect startups and MSMEs with markets and finance, we have launched initiatives like the Brics Incubator Network, the Brics MSME Portal, and the Brics Startup Innovation Fund,” PM Modi said.He urged businesses from Brics countries to use these platforms to increase the movement of investment, technology and talent across member economies.A major theme of PM Modi's address was economic resilience. The disruption of global supply chains in recent years, from the Covid-19 pandemic to geopolitical conflicts and trade tensions, has pushed countries to diversify sources of energy, technology, raw materials and manufactured goods.India, PM Modi said, has been working to make its supply chains more diversified and reliable.“The theme of India's Brics chairmanship is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability.' Over the past 12 years, India has made this mantra the foundation of its economic and trade policies,” he said.He pointed to India's efforts across sectors ranging from energy to technology, arguing that stronger and more diversified supply chains would help the economy withstand external shocks.“It is a result of this resilience that, even amidst global uncertainties, India today offers the assurance of growth and stability,” the PM said.The emphasis on resilience also reflects India's broader push to reduce vulnerabilities in strategically important sectors. The government has increasingly sought to build domestic manufacturing capacity while simultaneously attracting global companies looking to diversify production beyond existing manufacturing hubs.PM Modi highlighted infrastructure expansion as another pillar of India's economic strategy.India is rapidly expanding its network of roads, railways, ports and airports, he said, arguing that better physical connectivity is essential for lowering logistics costs and improving the movement of goods and people.At the same time, the government is trying to build domestic capabilities in technologies and industries that could have long-term economic and strategic importance.“We are rapidly expanding our roads, railways, ports, and airports. Simultaneously, we are building new capabilities in strategic sectors such as shipbuilding, semiconductors, quantum technology, critical minerals, and biotechnology,” PM Modi said.These sectors are increasingly important because they sit at the intersection of economic security and national security.Semiconductors, for example, are essential for everything from smartphones and automobiles to advanced weapons and artificial intelligence systems. Critical minerals are required for batteries, electronics and clean-energy technologies, while shipbuilding is important both for trade and maritime security.By expanding domestic capabilities in such areas, India is seeking to become not merely a large consumer market but a producer and supplier within global value chains.PM Modi also highlighted India's digital public infrastructure, particularly the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), as an example of how technology can expand economic participation.UPI has transformed the way payments are made in India by enabling fast digital transactions between bank accounts and mobile applications. PM Modi said the system has given fresh momentum to financial inclusion and digital payments on a massive scale.“Today, 50% of the world's real-time payments take place using this technology,” he said.India has increasingly sought to promote its digital infrastructure model internationally, particularly among developing economies. The broader objective is to demonstrate how digital systems can bring more people and businesses into the formal economy while making transactions faster and cheaper.The Brics Business Forum is the grouping's main private-sector platform, bringing together business leaders, government ministers and heads of state to discuss trade, investment, finance, technology and development.Its importance extends beyond discussions at individual meetings. Recommendations from the Brics Business Council and the Business Forum can feed into summit declarations and subsequent work programmes, giving the business community a role in shaping the bloc's economic agenda.The Leaders' Session in New Delhi was attended by Brics leaders, the Chairs of the Brics Business Council and the Brics Women's Business Alliance. Modi also joined the participating dignitaries for a group photograph.The forum is being held as India hosts the 18th Brics Summit under its 2026 chairship. India's presidency is centred on the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with development, sustainability and innovation among its principal priorities.Brics has expanded considerably from its original five-member format and now comprises 11 countries: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the UAE.Collectively, the grouping represents around 49.5% of the world's population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of global trade, according to background information on India's 2026 chairship.For India, the economic significance of Brics therefore goes beyond the traditional diplomatic role of the grouping. Its large consumer markets, energy producers, manufacturing economies and emerging technology sectors create opportunities for greater trade and investment.PM Modi's address sought to underline India's position within that changing economic landscape: as a country attempting to keep markets open, diversify supply chains, build strategic industrial capacity and use its digital infrastructure to expand economic participation.His broader pitch was that as geopolitical tensions and protectionism reshape global commerce, India wants to position itself as a reliable economic partner, one that can connect businesses, markets, investment and technology across an increasingly fragmented world.
Article Summary: Trade barriers rising globally, india building economic bridges: pm modi at brics business forum. India seeks deeper economic role within brics.supply-chain resilience becomes a key priority for india. Pm modi highlighted infrastructure expansion as another pillar of india's economic strategy.

Article Title: TOI Social Impact Summit 2026: Piyush Goyal calls for low-cost innovations to drive social impact
Article Text:
At the

TOI Social Impact Summit 2026

, government and business leaders discussed responsible growth,

sustainable business models

, philanthropy, ESG and the role of capital markets in creating social impact.

Sustainability must be part of the business model

Fair practices are central to responsible enterprise

Making sustainability work for business

Can the Social Stock Exchange transform social impact?

Building a culture of giving

Gold and the circular economy

Disclaimer: This article is part of a brand initiative by TOI in partnership with Malabar Gold & Diamonds and Reliance Foundation.

India needs affordable, locally developed solutions to address some of its most pressing social and environmental challenges, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said at the TOI Social Impact Summit 2026.Calling upon startups and innovators to develop cost-effective and sustainable technologies, Goyal referred to an ongoing lake rejuvenation initiative in his North Mumbai parliamentary constituency. He said India needed locally developed solutions such as low-cost machines for cleaning and maintaining water bodies."Machines are internationally available but at a huge price. Maybe one of our startups will very easily be able to make it," he said.Reflecting on India's CSR framework, Goyal said he had initially believed that mandatory CSR spending could weaken the country's traditional culture of voluntary giving."When the Companies Bill was piloted about 13-14 years ago, bringing in the provision of mandatory 2% spend on CSR, we were in opposition," he said. "I had felt we were actually doing a disservice to the Indian ethos, to the Indian way of life, because in India people do not do CSR out of compulsion."However, he acknowledged that the policy had brought more funds into social development.Goyal also said government welfare initiatives, including affordable housing, had restored dignity, created household assets and helped expand the middle class. Rising dual-income households and improved living standards, he added, were also contributing to economic growth."This is a very profitable proposition when you serve society," he said.BCCL COO Mohit Jain added that national growth must be assessed not merely through output, investment and ambition, but through the lives strengthened by development."A tree does not grow upward alone but underneath as well. So it is with the nation," Jain said. "The true strength of a country is revealed at its roots — in the student who gains access to better education, the patient who receives timely care and the community that becomes resilient enough to face an uncertain future."ITC Chairman and Managing Director Sanjiv Puri said sustainability and inclusive growth must be embedded in the corporate sector's business model."Economic progress cannot be seen in isolation from sustainability. Both have to go together," Puri said. "Corporates must create economic value, because that creates the foundation to go beyond. But it must be both economic and societal value. And that is what we call responsible competitiveness."He urged organisations to look beyond short-term shareholder value, pointing out that responsible business behaviour was increasingly being demanded by regulators, global trade bodies and conscious stakeholders.Puri said the world was facing a "perfect storm" of geopolitical turmoil, the weaponisation of tariffs and the climate crisis. These pressures, he noted, were affecting livelihoods, food security and nutrition, with vulnerable communities facing the greatest threat.He called for closer cooperation between the government, corporate sector and civil society to address climate change and support India's low-carbon growth trajectory.Citing ITC's own business model, Puri explained how the company had developed an ecosystem involving specialised research and development, the cultivation of climate-resilient trees requiring less water for its paperboards business, and partnerships with small farmers for its fruit juices operations.He also said CSR must be treated as a long-term business venture, with measurable outcomes and strong community capacity."You have to first invest in building capacity at the community level so that the initiatives are sustained and built upon. Otherwise, over a period of time, they wither away," he said.Speaking at the inaugural session, MP Ahammed, Chairman of the Malabar Group, said ethical business practices, local compliance and transparency were central to responsible growth.Malabar Gold & Diamonds, founded in Kozhikode over three decades ago, operates across. Ahammed said the group's operations were aligned with the vision of "Make in India, Market to the World."He identified quality, warranty and guarantee as the three core principles guiding the company's business. He also described employees as the company's "biggest assets," particularly those involved in crafting its jewellery.Ahammed announced that the Malabar Group would allocate Rs 200 crore, or 5% of its net trading profit, towards CSR initiatives in 2026-27.The key focus areas will include education, hunger alleviation, healthcare and women's empowerment. Its 'Hunger Free World' initiative aims to provide food to vulnerable communities and contribute towards eliminating starvation.The summit also featured a discussion on how companies are integrating sustainability into their core strategy, operations and investment decisions to create long-term value for stakeholders.The session, titled 'Making Sustainability Work for Business, and Business Work for Sustainability', featured Dr Neha Garyali, Vice-President, Centre of Excellence, VeARC Technologies, and Prabodha Acharya, Chief Sustainability Officer, JSW Group.The discussion placed sustainability within the wider context of business strategy, rather than treating it as a separate or standalone corporate responsibility function.Another session examined the role of India's Social Stock Exchange in helping social enterprises access capital and improve accountability.The discussion, titled 'From CSR to Capital Markets: Can India's Social Stock Exchange Transform Social Impact?', featured Mangesh Wange, Chief Executive Officer and Board Member, Swades Foundation; Riddhesh Shah, Deputy Vice-President, BSE; and Vineet Shastry, Associate Vice-President, NSE.The session looked at the relationship between social impact, capital markets and institutional participation, while examining whether new financial mechanisms can help scale organisations working on social challenges.At the session on philanthropy, volunteerism and collective action, Sumit Tayal, CEO of Give, highlighted the changing culture of giving in India."It is assumed that people start to give when they have made a lot of money, but 18- to 25-year-olds are giving as much as people older than them. Women make up 50% of donors," Tayal said.The discussion focused on how philanthropy can become more participatory and collective, with younger donors, women and volunteers playing a greater role in supporting social causes.Gold, India's second-largest import commodity by value, is increasingly becoming part of the domestic circular economy.The session on 'Circular and Responsible Gold Value Chains: Unlocking Social and Environmental Impact' examined responsible sourcing, recycling, organised credit and the financialisation of gold.Asher O, Managing Director – India Operations, Malabar Gold & Diamonds, said the company meets around 80% of its demand through people trading in their old gold.Kaushlendra Sinha, CEO of the Indian Association for Gold Excellence and Standards, said younger buyers were increasingly seeking information about the source of gold and demanding proof of responsible sourcing.Sachin Jain, Regional CEO India, World Gold Council, said responsible mining in India could help reduce excessive dependence on imports.Mayank Sharma, President and Head of Gold Loan at IIFL Finance, discussed the role of gold loans in improving credit access for households and MSMEs. Vikram Dhawan, Head Commodities and Fund Manager at Nippon India Mutual Fund, spoke about the growing financialisation of gold through gold ETFs.Together, the discussions highlighted the need for greater transparency, responsible mining, recycling and organised financial systems across the gold value chain.
Article Summary: India needs affordable, locally developed solutions to address some of its most pressing social and environmental challenges. Union minister of commerce and industry piyush goyal said he had initially believed that mandatory csr spending could weaken the country's traditional culture of voluntary giving.

Article Title: NPCI Bharat Bill Pay proposes new infra to fix MSME's collection problems
Article Text:
NPCI Bharat BillPay has proposed a centralised digital infrastructure to connect invoices, payments, reconciliation and financing, to fix the biggest constraints on MSMEs.

Mumbai:

NPCI Bharat BillPay has proposed a centralised digital infrastructure to connect invoices, payments, reconciliation and financing, to fix the biggest constraints on MSMEs - the difficulty of turning sales into cash and cash flows into credit.The system could help address the MSME sector’s Rs 60 lakh crore formal credit gap while reducing the friction involved in collecting and matching payments.The proposed infrastructure would digitise the order-to-cash cycle through standardised APIs and automate reconciliation across more than 20 crore monthly GST e-invoices. Buyer-confirmed invoices could become financeable records, allowing lenders to assess borrowers on the strength of their cash flows rather than relying only on collateral. A common information layer could also reduce the mismatches that contribute to delays in MSME receivables.According to a report by NPCI Bharat BillPay and Bain & Company, formal credit of around Rs 34 lakh crore meets only part of an estimated Rs 92 lakh crore demand for MSME debt, leaving a gap of around Rs 60 lakh crore. The shortage is greatest among smaller enterprises, where formal channels meet only 30% to 40% of debt demand.Payment delays add to the problem. Around Rs 8.1 lakh crore of MSME receivables remain locked up in delayed payments, according to the report. Finance teams spend 30% to 40% of their time on reconciliation and transaction matching, including invoice processing, payment follow-ups and exception handling.The underlying problem is less a lack of digital components than their inability to talk to one another. India has digitised many parts of its business ecosystem, but fragmented information flows between platforms continue to impose costs on businesses and restrict their access to capital.Bain & Company partner Saurabh Trehan said the next stage of B2B digitisation would require greater connectivity between business systems, payment providers, banks, financiers and public systems. “India's next chapter of B2B transformation is not only about moving money faster; it is about making the underlying transaction visible, verifiable, and actionable across the ecosystem,” he said.The proposed layer would provide the common infrastructure for these connections. Advanced analytics and agentic AI could then be built on top of it, providing cash-flow intelligence, dynamic risk scoring, agentic credit underwriting and open-market intelligence.NBBL MD & CEO Noopur Chaturvedi said interoperability would be central to B2B commerce as businesses digitise their operations. “The future of B2B commerce will be built on interoperability,” she said. A standardised and connected system could link invoices, payments, reconciliation and financing while improving access to credit for underserved MSMEs, she said.The opportunity extends beyond credit. India’s formal business sector is worth more than Rs 130 lakh crore and contributes around 45% of the country’s GVA, according to the report. A connected digital ecosystem is identified as one of four enablers that could help raise the sector’s productivity.
Article Summary: Npci bharat billpay has proposed a centralised digital infrastructure to connect invoices, payments, reconciliation and financing. System could help address the msme sector’s rs 60 lakh crore formal credit gap while reducing the friction involved in collecting and matching payments.

Article Title: Algorithms should be able to explain reasoning behind decisions to customers: RBI Murmu
Article Text:
RBI deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu, speaking at the Global FinTech Fest in Mumbai on Friday, said digital lending should not merely make the process of extending credit faster.

Mumbai:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Reserve Bank of India wants lenders to ensure that algorithms used to make or materially influence credit decisions can explain why a borrower has been rejected, putting accountability and explainability at the centre of its expectations for technology-driven lending.RBI deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu, speaking at the Global FinTech Fest in Mumbai on Friday, said digital lending should not merely make the process of extending credit faster. Technology and better data should help lenders reach borrowers who have historically remained outside the formal financial system, making credit “better” as well as faster."The vendor with the printed QR code is now part of the formal financial system. The questions she faces next are harder ones. Will she be offered credit on terms she can understand? If an algorithm declines her 10 application, will anyone be able to tell her why? If her account is frozen by a frauddetection system, how long before she can trade again? Those questions are the real content of trusted innovation, and how we answer them will matter more than any technology we deploy," said Murmu.The deputy governor also cautioned institutions against being comfortable with their cryptographic dependencies.He said that while quantum computing is not an immediate threat payment infrastructure has long tech cycles and migration to new standards takes years. "There is also the “harvest now, decrypt later” risk, under which encrypted information collected today becomes accessible as computing capability advance," said Murmu.The challenge is particularly relevant for India's millions of small merchants who have moved into the formal digital payments system. The RBI's concern is that algorithms can produce decisions that are statistically effective without being readily understandable. Murmu said well-designed models could identify creditworthy borrowers who might otherwise remain outside formal finance, but warned that the data used by such models could contain historical biases. Past relationships may not persist, a model may be economically inappropriate despite its statistical sophistication, and complex models may be difficult to explain to a customer whose application has been declined.The RBI's position is also that automation does not transfer responsibility from the lender to the technology. “The answer cannot be the algorithm,” Murmu said when asking who is accountable when an algorithm makes or materially influences a financial decision. Responsibility, he said, rests with the regulated institution, while boards and senior management must understand the models they deploy, their limitations and the consequences of using them.This principle extends to the wider digital-lending ecosystem. Under the RBI's Digital Lending Directions, 2025, technology can change the channel through which credit is delivered but does not dilute the responsibility of the regulated lender. Borrowers must know who is lending to them, the cost of the loan and its terms, while technology should widen customer choice rather than steer borrowers towards unsuitable products. Even when lenders operate through partnerships, the regulated entity remains accountable for services delivered in its name.
Article Summary: Rbi deputy governor shirish chandra murmu spoke at the global fintech fest in mumbai. He said digital lending should not merely make the process of extending credit faster. Technology and better data should help lenders reach borrowers who have historically remained outside the formal financial system, he said.

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the us-iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: How Aryna Sabalenka’s fiancé Georgios Frangulis built his own empire before becoming her biggest supporter
Article Text:
Georgios Frangulis and Aryna Sabalenka (Getty Images)

Who is Georgios Frangulis, Aryna Sabalenka 's fiancé?

Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis (Getty Images)

How did Georgios Frangulis build Oakberry into a global brand?

When did Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis start dating?

How did Georgios Frangulis propose to Aryna Sabalenka?

What is 'The Gride,' Georgios Frangulis's new fashion brand?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Long before he was cheering from the players' box at Grand Slams, Georgios Frangulis was building something of his own. The Brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called Oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business with more than 800 stores across 50 countries. Now 37, Frangulis proposed to world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in March 2026, capping a relationship that began when she signed on as an Oakberry brand ambassador in early 2024.Born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil, Frangulis has Greek roots, with his family originally from Thessaloniki, Greece. He studied law at FAAP -- Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado -- in 2014, but never sat the bar exam."I always knew I wouldn't be a lawyer," he said. "What I really wanted was to be an entrepreneur."That clarity of purpose was rare at the time. Most people spend years hedging. Frangulis walked away from a law degree, moved to the United States, where he became infatuated with açaí, came back to São Paulo, and launched Oakberry in December 2016.Co-founded alongside Renato Haidar, Oakberry was not just another smoothie shop. Frangulis positioned açaí as functional nutrition -- clean ingredients, no artificial syrups, and a strong link to fitness culture -- and built a franchise model designed from day one to scale internationally.The company raised $67 million in capital in late 2023. By mid-2026, Oakberry had grown to a 900-location global business, with stores in Dubai malls, Miami gyms, Australian beach towns, and European city centres -- all without compromising brand consistency.In June 2023, Frangulis graced the cover of Forbes Brazil. The profile explored not just his entrepreneurial arc but his spirituality and Greek identity. His bicep tattoo reads "Fight for us, Saint George the Warrior." His forearm reads, "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." These are not the accessories of a brand persona.His net worth in 2026 is estimated between $75 million and $100 million -- built almost entirely from his equity in Oakberry, not from market listings or quick exits.They met in January 2024 when Sabalenka was hired as an ambassador for Oakberry. The couple were first spotted together in April 2024 -- a month after the tragic and untimely death of Sabalenka's ex-boyfriend, Konstantin Koltsov, who died by suicide in March 2024.It was a difficult period, and Sabalenka has been open about what Frangulis meant to her during it. "There was a really tough period where I was really happy to have him by my side, always cheering me up, always making sure that we are doing some fun stuff," she told People. "His support means so much to me. Being on the road and having him support me, to make me laugh and to be able to work out together, makes life on the road feel more like home. "Sabalenka had been broadly hinting for months. After winning the Brisbane International in January 2026, she said in her victory speech: "Thank you to my boyfriend... Hopefully soon I can call you something else, right? Let's just put some extra pressure."Frangulis proposed to Sabalenka in Indian Wells, California, on March 3, 2026. The setting was candlelit, with rose petals arranged beside a pool -- a rental home the couple had spent time in since the early days of their relationship. Sabalenka, in jeans and a white t-shirt, had no idea it was coming."I always knew I wanted to propose to Aryna because I was 100% sure she was the person I wanted to spend the rest of my life with," he shared in a YouTube video about the moment.The ring was designed by Isabela Grutman, who worked with Frangulis for months to create the custom piece. It features a 12-carat, oval-cut diamond surrounded by emeralds set in platinum -- Sabalenka's favorite stone, and also her birthstone. Experts told InStyle the ring could be worth up to $1 million. They captioned their joint Instagram post: "You & me, forever."Earlier in 2026, Frangulis launched his own fashion brand, named The Gride. The name honors his Greek heritage and mixes the words Greek and Pride. "My pride comes from my grandparents and has spread to my closest circle," the brand's website states. "The feeling is unmatched, and I'll do my best to make each and every one of you feel it too."Outside business, Frangulis races Porsche GT3 Cup cars. "Getting in the car and racing is one of the few moments when nothing else matters," he told Forbes Brazil. For someone whose professional life spans dozens of countries and time zones, that says something about how he recharges.What is clear is that Frangulis arrived in this relationship with his own story already written. He built a global company from a fruit most of the world had never heard of, then quietly showed up for the woman he loves at every stop on the tour. That is not a supporting role. It is just a different kind of ambition.
Article Summary: Georgios frangulis proposed to world no. 1 aryna sabalenka in march 2026. The brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business with more than 800 stores. Frangulis proposed to sabalenka in a candlelit setting at a rental home.

Article Title: California governor signs law to limit U-16s social media risks
Article Text:
Gavin Newsom

California governor Gavin Newsom signed more than a dozen new laws on Thursday that address various aspects of children's safety online, including one that prohibits social media companies from serving addictive features to users under 16 years old. During a signing ceremony, Newsom described the restrictions as "better" than Australia's ban for all users under 16."This is about the features themselves. This is about addressing the substantive issue around the engineering. If you address that, then the age issue is not the essential issue," Newsom said. The new law defines "addictive" features as ones that are "psychologically exploitative" and prohibits social media companies from providing children with features such as infinite scroll, algorithmic recommendations and autoplay.

Article Title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max get Variable Aperture as 'most important' camera feature: What it means for users
Article Text:
Apple iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max

Aperture is the part of a camera most phone users never see

The useful bit is what happens when you take control

It is not just about low light

The aperture is only on one camera

Apple is adding more control to video too

The idea isn't new to smartphones

The bigger camera change is the combination

What variable aperture actually changes for iPhone users

Apple has added variable aperture to the main camera on both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. This will offer users a physical way to control how much light reaches the sensor for the first time on an iPhone.The feature sits alongside a new 48MP Fusion Main camera, a redesigned sensor and new Pro Controls. Apple says the six laser-cut blades inside the lens can move between four aperture settings, while the camera can also adjust the aperture automatically depending on the scene.That sounds like a minor hardware upgrade. But it is not. The lens opening affects exposure, depth of field, and how motion is captured, so giving the iPhone aperture control adds something software alone can't quite duplicate.Apple's description is straightforward: "iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48 megapixel fusion main camera with variable aperture for creative control that wasn't possible before," Apple said. "This is the most advanced camera we've ever made."Aperture is simply the opening through which light passes before reaching a camera's image sensor. It is measured using f-numbers such as f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8 and f/4.0.The lower the f-number, the wider the opening and the more light reaches the sensor.A wider aperture can therefore help in darker conditions. A narrower aperture lets in less light, but it also keeps more of the scene in focus.Most smartphone cameras use a fixed aperture. The lens has one opening, and the phone relies heavily on shutter speed, ISO, and computational photography to handle different lighting conditions.The iPhone 18 Pro changes that for its main camera. Its lens can open as wide as f/1.48 and then stop down to f/1.8, f/2.8 or f/4.0. Six blades inside the lens physically change the opening size.Apple says the blades are laser-cut and thinner than a human hair. They are designed to move smoothly between the available settings rather than simply switching between two fixed positions.The camera can make that decision automatically. In a darker scene, it can open the aperture to f/1.48 and let in more light. In brighter conditions, it can narrow the opening.For most people, the automatic system will do most of the work. The Camera app can choose an aperture based on the scene, just as it already decides on exposure and other settings.The difference is that iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max owners can also take control themselves.Apple's new Pro Controls let users manually change aperture, shutter speed, and white balance. A histogram can also be displayed to help judge exposure across a scene.That gives photographers another way to decide how a picture should look, instead of leaving every exposure decision to the camera.The most obvious example is depth of field. At a wider aperture such as f/1.48, the camera can produce more optical background blur when the subject is relatively close and the background is farther away.Stopping down to f/4.0 has the opposite effect. More of the scene can stay in focus, which can help with landscapes or group photos where people stand at different distances from the camera.That matters because a group shot can otherwise leave one person sharp while another, standing slightly farther away, falls outside the plane of focus. A narrower aperture gives the camera more room to keep those subjects in focus.It also gives photographers another option when deliberately introducing motion into an image. A narrower aperture reduces the amount of light entering the lens, making it easier to use a slower shutter speed when conditions are bright enough.The obvious benefit of opening the aperture is light. Apple says the main camera can open to ƒ/1.48 for low-light photography, letting more light reach the sensor.That can give the camera more flexibility before it has to compensate by increasing ISO or slowing the shutter speed. In practical terms, that can help preserve detail and reduce noise, while a fast enough shutter can keep moving subjects sharp.But variable aperture is useful in the opposite direction too.In bright daylight, photographers sometimes want a slower shutter speed to create motion blur. That can be useful with moving water, people, or cars, and it also matters in video, where shutter speed is normally tied to frame rate.A fixed wide aperture can make that difficult in strong sunlight because too much light reaches the sensor even when the shutter is already operating at its fastest useful setting. Stopping the lens down gives the camera another way to reduce exposure.There are limits, though. A range ending at f/4.0 does not eliminate the need for neutral-density filters in every bright-light situation. Photographers who want long exposures in direct sunlight may still need an ND filter to cut the light further.Apple's implementation has an important limitation. The variable aperture is on the main 24mm camera. It does not extend across the entire rear camera system.The ultra-wide and telephoto cameras don't have the same variable-aperture mechanism. That means the new optical control is available only when shooting through the main lens.This is also why the feature should not be viewed as a replacement for the other cameras or for computational photography. Exposure, autofocus, HDR, noise reduction and image processing still determine much of the final photograph.The hardware simply gives the camera another physical variable to work with before those processes take over.Aperture changes also feed into Apple's video features. The new Pro Controls work with video as well as photography, letting users manually adjust settings including aperture and shutter speed. That is especially relevant for people who want more predictable exposure rather than letting the phone change settings during recording.Apple has also added the ability to apply Cinematic effects after capture to videos recorded at up to 60 frames per second. That means users can make this adjustment after recording instead of committing to the effect while shooting.Time-lapse recording now supports 4K and Dolby Vision HDR, while Audio Mix has new algorithms designed to improve voice quality and isolate music.The combination is notable because Apple isn't presenting the variable aperture as an isolated camera specification. It is part of a broader attempt to give users more control over how photos and video are captured and processed.Apple is not the first phone maker to put a variable aperture in a smartphone. Samsung introduced a dual-aperture system with the Galaxy S9 series in 2018. That system switched between f/1.5 and f/2.4 depending on the lighting conditions.Huawei later introduced more flexible variable-aperture systems, while Xiaomi and Honor have also used the technology in flagship phones.The reason it has remained relatively uncommon is fairly simple: fitting a mechanical aperture mechanism into a smartphone camera adds complexity to an already tightly packed module.For years, phone makers instead concentrated on larger sensors, multiple cameras and computational photography. Those technologies can compensate for many of the limitations of a fixed aperture without adding moving parts to the lens.The iPhone 18 Pro's approach is therefore less about replacing computational photography than adding an optical control alongside it.The variable aperture gets most of the attention, but Apple has made several other changes to the camera system.The 48MP Fusion Main camera uses a new sensor and a new computational imaging pipeline that Apple says produces sharper, more detailed images. Photographic Styles now include additional texture and grain controls, giving users more ways to change the look of their photos.Apple has also added persistent subject tracking for photos and video, letting the camera keep following a person even if they temporarily disappear behind someone else in a crowd.Another feature aimed at photographers is Apple Reference Image. When Reference mode is used, the camera captures signed sensor data that Private Cloud Compute turns into what Apple describes as an "unalterable reference image." You can then view the reference alongside the main photograph in the Photos app.The idea is to compare the original sensor-derived reference with the photograph and identify whether changes have been made. Apple says the feature is intended to address image authenticity, particularly for photographers and photojournalists.Apple is also adding metadata support and upcoming support for the SynthID standard to help identify images generated or edited with AI.For someone who simply opens the Camera app and takes pictures, it may not change much. The phone can choose the aperture automatically, just as it already handles most exposure decisions. For people who shoot deliberately, the change is more useful.A wider f/1.48 setting can help in darker scenes. Stopping down can keep more of a group or landscape in focus. Manual aperture control can also be combined with shutter-speed control to create particular motion effects.It can even produce optical effects that fixed-aperture smartphone cameras cannot reproduce in the same way, including changes in how bright points of light appear at narrower apertures.But four aperture settings don't turn the iPhone into a dedicated interchangeable-lens camera. The sensor remains small compared with most conventional cameras, and the amount of natural optical background blur depends heavily on the distance between the camera, subject, and background.For many portraits, Apple's computational Portrait mode will still produce a stronger and more controllable background-blur effect.The same is true for long exposures in bright daylight. The f/1.48-to-f/4.0 range gives photographers more room, but it does not remove the physical limits imposed by available light.That is probably the right way to look at the iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture. It gives the camera one more physical control over exposure and focus, while the sensor and software continue to determine what ultimately reaches the screen.For casual users, most of that will happen automatically. For photographers and videographers who want to decide how the shot is captured, the four aperture settings and Pro Controls make the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max considerably more flexible than a fixed-aperture iPhone.
Article Summary: Aperture is the opening through which light passes before reaching a camera's image sensor. Six blades inside the lens physically change the opening size. Apple says the blades are laser-cut and thinner than a human hair. They are designed to move smoothly between the available settings.

Article Title: ARC raises Rs 10.5 crore in pre-seed funding
Article Text: ARC, a gaming technology company has raised Rs 10.5 crore in pre‑seed funding led by Chimera VC and MIXI Global Investments, with participation from Dhruv Vohra, Director, Meta, APAC, in his personal capacity. The funding will accelerate development and commercialisation of ARC X1, covering hardware engineering, product validation, manufacturing readiness, and further development of OWL OS and ARC’s gaming software platform. It will also support team expansion, go‑to‑market capabilities, and strategic partnerships across gaming, cloud, content and technology.The global portable gaming console market was valued at US$3.89 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow at 9.7% CAGR through 2033. ARC aims to tap into India’s large mobile‑first gaming community and the low penetration of dedicated gaming hardware, creating space for a more accessible portable gaming category.Founded by Jobin Joseph and Kaustubh K. Jadhav, ARC is building a platform that integrates hardware, software and gaming experiences. The ARC X1 is a portable gaming system designed to make dedicated gaming more accessible to Indian gamers.ARC is developing its own hardware and software stack, aiming to build an ecosystem across devices, operating systems, software services and gaming experiences.Joseph said the funding will deepen ARC’s technology, accelerate product development and move the company closer to launch. Jadhav added that ARC was founded on the belief that access should not determine how deeply someone experiences gaming, and the funding will help bring ARC X1 to gamers at scale.Chimera VC’s Krish Anurag said ARC fits their thesis of backing companies that can become infrastructure for the next chapter of gaming. MIXI Global Investments’ Tomoharu Urabe said ARC X1 can make handheld gaming more accessible for India’s passionate gaming community.ARC X1 is built on ARM architecture, powered by Qualcomm technology, and runs OWL OS, ARC’s proprietary gaming operating system. It supports native Android gaming, PC‑game compatibility through ARC’s software stack, and cloud gaming. ARC has crossed 50,000 waitlist sign‑ups and collaborated with Qualcomm ahead of launch, adopting a community‑led development model involving gamers through early testing and feedback programmes.
Article Summary: Arc, a gaming technology company has raised rs 10.5 crore in pre‑seed funding. The funding will accelerate development and commercialisation of arc x1. Arc aims to tap into india’s large mobile‑first gaming community and the low penetration of dedicated gaming hardware.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu warns companies against sharing sensitive data with AI labs: This is quite serious and …
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu raises AI data security concerns

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has raised concerns about the growing use of frontier AI models by companies handling sensitive information. Quoting Fields Medalist Terence Tao, Sridhar Vembu shared an X (formerly Twitter) post that said companies with critical know-how, intellectual property and trade secrets should be careful about trusting their information with frontier AI labs. The mathematician warned that AI could change how researchers share ideas. Tao said, "The incentives may now be pointing in the direction of no longer sharing any promising research directions with the broader community, which would reverse centuries of traditions of open science and do serious long-term damage to the future of the field".Sridhar Vembu said companies with valuable intellectual property and trade secrets should be cautious about putting their information into frontier AI systems. "This is quite serious and it is not just mathematicians and scientists," Vembu wrote.He argued that the concern could apply to companies across industries that have sensitive information they do not want to expose outside their organisations.In the post, Vembu also highlighted the pharmaceutical industry as an example. He said major pharma companies already have their own AI models, often based on open-source models, to avoid giving large AI companies information about new drug molecules and processes they are developing."That caution is well warranted," Sridhar Vembu said.Zoho founder says companies should build their own AI models"Your company's know-how belongs in your own AI model," Vembu wrote. He also said that building and running private AI models is becoming easier and cheaper. “Fortunately they are easy to train and becoming cheaper to run too”.
Article Summary: Sridhar vembu raises ai data security concerns over frontier ai. He said companies with critical know-how, intellectual property and trade secrets should be careful about trusting their information with frontier ai labs. The mathematician warned that ai could change how researchers share ideas.
